races.name: Paul Kavanagh Memorial AJA Novice Flat Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes (For Jockeys With Three Wins Or Fewer At Start Of Season)

runners_data.name: Pedro The Poet
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards runner dropping back from 10-12f trips where he has consistently faded late, and his Good-ground sim record of 0 wins and 0 places from 3 runs offers no encouragement; 93 days off the track is an additional concern at 5yo in this company.

runners_data.name: Epidavros
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's runner has five consecutive fourth-or-worse finishes in Good-ground handicaps and is a natural rear-of-field operator quietly shuffled into a midfield slot by weight of numbers — his best chance rests on getting closer to the pace than his instincts usually allow.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 7yo has a place from 12f on Good ground and is naturally inclined to race from the back, though the redistribution means he will need to take a more forward pitch than usual; a recent run 17 days ago leaves him fit and he is one of the more credible hold-up threats here.

runners_data.name: Titian
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 8yo has a clear Good-ground preference with a win and a place from seven similar-going runs, but consecutive poor efforts at 10f on Good suggest he has gone off the boil; amateur jockey Mr Loughnane has three or fewer wins and the headgear flag (p) adds a small wild-card element.

runners_data.name: Up The Jazz
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey runner has an excellent Good-ground profile — 1 win and 4 places from 10 runs on the surface — and ran just 13 days ago, suggesting peak fitness; racing from a hold-up position she will need to track up closer than usual if Sanafi Zabeel's pace is modest, but she represents one of the strongest form profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 5yo is the race's only confirmed front-runner and has won over 8f on Good ground, posting a sim-going record of 2 wins and 5 places from 9 runs — the outstanding pace-figure in this field; Miss Williams will look to exploit an unchallenged lead from the outset.

runners_data.name: Eagles Dream
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 4yo has missed the frame in all five recent starts including runs of 8th and 11th, and as a true hold-up horse pressed into a midfield map position, the distance step back to 9f from longer trips adds further uncertainty; the lowest OR in the field at 58 reflects the current level.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 11yo ran just 3 days ago — the shortest gap of any runner here — and carries top weight at 142lbs despite an OR of 52; an all-weather specialist with zero wins or places on Good ground from 15 sim-going runs, and racing wide of her natural hold-up zone.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's 5yo boasts a striking 5 places from 15 Good-ground runs despite winning nothing, showing he can get into a race without converting; as the field's lightest weighted runner and a horse whose best distance has been 10-12f, stepping down to 9f on a pace-controlled day may not unlock his best.

races.paceDynamic: Sanafi Zabeel is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of nine and should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over this 1m1f trip at Carlisle, setting a comfortable, self-regulated gallop on Good ground. With no rival likely to seriously dispute the early lead, Sanafi Zabeel can control the tempo entirely, which at Carlisle — a track that rewards prominent runners who can save ground on the bend — is a meaningful structural advantage. The rest of the field is dominated by hold-up types forced to chase from off the pace, and with no pressure likely through the first half of the race, the pace could be modest enough to blunt the finish of genuine closers. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or very close prominent horse who can dictate and resist the late challenge, rather than a deep hold-up profile that needs a truly searching gallop to set up a late run. Five horses — Epidavros, Spirit Catcher, Eagles Dream, Jewel Maker and On The Bubble — are redistributed true hold-up types shown in midfield because the map cannot accommodate so many rear-runners; of these, Spirit Catcher and Epidavros, with higher ORs and better recent form, are best placed to actually secure a forward enough position to matter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sanafi Zabeel Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sanafi Zabeel takes up the lead unopposed and sets a controlled, honest pace that leaves rivals with too little to chase.
scenarios.body: Sanafi Zabeel dictates from the front on form that includes a win over 8f on Good ground, and with no genuine pressurer in the field the pace will be entirely on her terms. A moderate gallop into the Carlisle home straight suits a front-runner who can quicken from a controlled position rather than the field's many hold-up horses who will need far more pace to be seen to best advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned just off the leader at the top of the straight has enough in reserve to reel in Sanafi Zabeel inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With Sanafi Zabeel controlling a modest pace, a horse travelling prominently and saving ground through the bend could pick up the winner's slipstream before striking late. Up The Jazz, whose Good-ground form shows consistent top-two finishes over shorter, and Epidavros, nudged forward from a natural hold-up role, are the most likely candidates to apply that challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough — perhaps through early jostling from redistributed types — to flatten the front-runner and leave the race open to a finisher.
scenarios.body: Under this shape a true closer gets the strong gallop they need, but this field's hold-up horses are largely redistributed riders racing out of role, which meaningfully reduces the probability of a clean late surge materialising. Spirit Catcher or Titian, the pick of the genuine hold-up profile, would be the beneficiaries if the fractions quicken sufficiently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Ties Up, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Sanafi Zabeel's early fractions prove too quick for the distance and she ties up in the straight, opening a scrambled finish.
scenarios.body: A breakdown in pace control could compress the field and produce a messy finish where form lines blur and the lowest-weighted runners with fresh legs are competitive. Eagles Dream and On The Bubble are lightly weighted outsiders who could profit from positional chaos, though their overall profile and redistribution status make this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Sanafi Zabeel's early pace — watch whether she quickens away cleanly or allows the field to bunch behind her, as the entire race shape pivots on whether she controls the gallop or gets crowded off the front end.
Up The Jazz's positioning — if Miss Clarkson gets her tracking Sanafi Zabeel within two lengths by halfway, she becomes the primary danger to the leader given her superior Good-ground place record.

Epidavros and Spirit Catcher at the start — both are true hold-up horses being pushed into midfield by field composition, and if either settles too far back they will have too much ground to make up against a leader setting a controlled pace.

Pedro The Poet's finishing run — watch for signs of his habitual fading in the final two furlongs, which would confirm the race is not truly end-to-end and that front-end horses are finding it easier than the pace map might suggest.

Eagles Dream's early behaviour — at 33 days between runs and with a pattern of wide, out-of-contention finishes, any signs of greenness or sluggish jumping-off could confirm this runner as a non-factor and reinforce the one-pace front-runner narrative.

races.name: Celebrating National Racehorse Week 2026 EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Colin Parker Raceday 1st Nov Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Kanzi
runners_data.note: Has form figures of 2-1 over 7-8f on good ground and handles this surface confidently; the step to 1m looks straightforward on breeding, and Callum Shepherd's booking for Charlie Johnston's yard (6/41 in 14 days) carries some clout — primary danger to the pace-setter if he can slot in behind from stall.|

runners_data.name: Bincimbal
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's 2-year-old arrives with 3-4-1 form, including a win at 7f on good, and is genuinely a front-running type forced into an artificial midfield role by sheer weight of pace in this field; that positional compromise materially dents his winning prospects here despite solid form credentials.|

runners_data.name: Ten Clarets
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's confirmed pace-setter has run three times on good ground and shapes as the ideal race-controller at 1m with no rival to press her; the 35-day break is a mild flag but Burke freshens horses well, and Pierre-Louis Jamin's retention suggests stable confidence — STYLE_FIT adjustment is only relevant if rivals actively contest the lead.|

runners_data.name: Emerald Bay
runners_data.note: George Scott's 2-year-old is in outstanding form — wins at 7f and 8f on good ground plus a blinker assist — and the two recent victories give him the strongest recent form profile in the race; pulled back to the rear by redistribution logic but his genuine staying profile at 8f means the 1m trip is a genuine asset rather than a concern.|

runners_data.name: Aurora Valkyrie
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's filly has modest form figures (8-5-3-7), has not won, and sits at OR 60 as the lowest-rated runner; she is a front-running type shuffled into midfield by the congested pace picture, meaning she is doubly disadvantaged — both by the positional compromise and by raw ability relative to these rivals.|

races.paceDynamic: Ten Clarets is the confirmed front runner and, with only five runners in this 1m nursery handicap at Carlisle, she is likely to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested gallop on good ground — dictating her own fractions without any genuine pressure from behind. Bincimbal and Aurora Valkyrie are both naturally prominent-minded types but are mapped into midfield because the field cannot accommodate three horses on the pace simultaneously; Kanzi and Emerald Bay complete a field where virtually every runner wants to be near the front. This creates a race where the pace is sustainable rather than pressured, a flat even-tempo mile that will likely set up a straight-line stamina test rather than a sprint for home — conditions that suit horses who can travel smoothly in behind before asserting, rather than true finishers with a late kick. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Ten Clarets is most likely to actually lead, with Kanzi the likeliest to slot into second, leaving Bincimbal and Aurora Valkyrie having to adapt and settle further off the pace than they prefer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ten Clarets Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Ten Clarets gets a clean break and controls a steady pace unchallenged throughout the mile.
scenarios.body: She sets a comfortable gallop on good ground, conserves energy through the long Carlisle straight, and kicks on from 2f out before rivals can organise their challenges; K.R. Burke's record with prominent types who dominate small fields supports this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Assert
scenarios.trigger: If Kanzi tracks Ten Clarets tightly and the pair pull clear of those forced back into unnatural midfield positions.
scenarios.body: Kanzi, switching to 1m on a sound surface with a win and place already on fast ground, sits a length off the leader and picks her off in the final furlong; the two naturally pace-committed horses dictate a race from which the redistributed midfielders cannot respond quickly enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Run From Emerald Bay
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slightly stronger than expected, Emerald Bay's forcing ride in a headgear-fitted, form-forward run (three wins from six, two recent) allows him to close strongly.
scenarios.body: Emerald Bay, who has won twice at 7-8f on good ground this season and whose barnstorming form figures of 113 indicate a horse in career-best form, benefits from any rare scenario where pace forces a faster early tempo; P.J. McDonald is well positioned to deliver a late thrust from a horse mapped to the rear but capable of genuine hold-up running.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the front-runners burn each other off, creating an improbable vacuum for the redistributed prominent types arriving from midfield.
scenarios.body: This shape is inherently unlikely because Bincimbal and Aurora Valkyrie are not true closers — both are front-runners forced back and would be racing entirely out of role to mount a late run; Aurora Valkyrie's form string (8537) offers little encouragement even in this unlikely shape.

watchPoints.text: Ten Clarets sets the tempo entirely alone — watch whether Pierre-Louis Jamin allows her to coast or pushes for an early advantage, as the pace she sets will define whether the midfield horses can close or not.

Bincimbal and Aurora Valkyrie are both naturally prominent types who will instinctively want to press forward at the start — a crowded early break could see unexpected jostling for position in a field where almost every runner wants the same ground.

Emerald Bay is fitted with a hood (headgear noted) and is in sharp form; watch his early behaviour under P.J. McDonald — if he settles better than his redistributed rear position implies, he is the most dangerous horse in the field on raw form figures.

With only five runners on good ground at Carlisle, the 1m trip is run on a relatively flat, fair track — any horse that jumps cleanly and gets an uninterrupted run is unlikely to be beaten for ground, so draw and barrier behaviour at the start deserves close attention.

races.name: Christmas Community Raceday 13th Dec Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rogue Attraction
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Bethell and Tudhope, who combine well; ran twice on Good over 6f this season for a win and a place — going and trip are squarely in her favour, and the headgear flag (hg:p) suggests she needs things to fall right late.|

runners_data.name: Invincible Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid Good-ground placed form at 6f; Fahey yard in fair form (T14: 6/45) and Barry McHugh booked; drew well in similar company before and may be able to sit just off the contested pace and challenge.|

runners_data.name: Rikki Tiki Tavi
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who carries a clear 'fades in finish' flag — the form string of consecutive zeros is brutal and no wins beyond a lower-grade 5f maiden; difficult to trust even if the shape theoretically suits a closer.|

runners_data.name: Here Forever
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner who will fight Town Queen for the lead; Barron stable is not firing (T14: 0/6), 52 days off the track, but the horse's sim-going record of 6/6 at this trip and going shows she handles conditions well — the pace duel may just cost her late.|

runners_data.name: Go Vince Go
runners_data.note: Busy prominent racer for Easterby (T14: 4/88), only 12 days since last run and returning quickly; 6f Good is his bread and butter (sim-going: 10/15) and recent 3rd at 6f Good shows he stays competitive at this level.|

runners_data.name: Tip Foster
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced prominent type with only two runs — a win over 7f Good and a 3rd over 6f Soft; Beasley and the Barron stable (same trainer as Here Forever, T14: 0/6) is a note of caution, but the raw form is good and 83 days off could mean improvement on handicap debut.|

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with headgear flag; all five sim-going runs on Good have produced minor form only (1W3P but OR 76), drops back from 7-8f to 6f which is a slight question; Callum Shepherd capable but horse needs to find more than recent runs suggest.|

runners_data.name: Town Queen
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will contest the lead with Here Forever; unbeaten in 1 (AW at Southwell) and placed three times, largely over 7f Good — dropping back to 6f on turf Good is a query, and 70 days off adds risk; Burke in form (T14: 6/40) is the key positive.|

runners_data.name: Kody B
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by inclination — mapped to midfield here because the field's rear positions are saturated with closers; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that he is unlikely to get the late-running position he needs, and his last four runs have produced nothing better than 4th at this level.|

runners_data.name: Trust Amy
runners_data.note: Another deep closer who has been slotted into midfield on the map rather than the rear because too many hold-up types compete for the same space; her simulated-going record of just 3/11 on Good is poor, and without a clear run from the back this is a difficult race to win.|

races.paceDynamic: Here Forever and Town Queen are the two confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the outset over Carlisle's 6f on Good turf, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a soft, uncontested gallop. That honest fractions scenario sets up a race run at a true clip throughout, which on a flat 6f track historically drains the pace-setters late and opens the race for those travelling just off the speed. Tip Foster and Go Vince Go sit in the prominent group and are best-placed to exploit any fade from the leading duo in the final furlong, while Invincible Boy offers another prominent angle with claims. The field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate cleanly — Kody B and Trust Amy are genuine deep closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the true rear-of-field berths are oversubscribed; those two are unlikely to secure their preferred late-running position in this contested-pace shape. The race shape favours prominent racers who can sit close enough to the early pace to pounce when the leaders inevitably tire, rather than true hold-up types who will face a timing and positional challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Here Forever and Town Queen fight for the front and set a genuine honest gallop that burns them both out inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The hot pace drains both pace-setters before the line and hands the advantage to horses travelling just behind them with energy in reserve; Tip Foster and Go Vince Go are ideally positioned to swoop from the prominent group and hit the line hardest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Here Forever (or Town Queen) gains a controlling lead and sets only a moderate pace, allowing a front-runner to conserve enough to outstay rivals.
scenarios.body: With the pace softened and no one able to force a true test, the leader bounces off Good ground in comfort and proves too strong for those held up; Here Forever's record of five wins and places at this trip and going makes her the obvious beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is ferocious enough that it creates genuine end-to-end attrition and the hold-up horses find a clear passage late.
scenarios.body: Rogue Attraction and Zarvali, tracking from midfield, would be first beneficiaries if the field strings out and gaps appear; however, the redistribution of Kody B and Trust Amy means the true deep closers may not find their natural position, limiting the late charge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Form Wins
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner commits fully early and the race defaults to a steadier gallop with a late sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A steady tempo suits horses with a sharp finishing kick rather than pure stamina; Invincible Boy's placed form on Good ground over 6f makes him a credible beneficiary, with Rogue Attraction also possessing the acceleration to exploit a sprint-to-the-line scenario.

watchPoints.text: Here Forever and Town Queen will lock horns for the lead from the off — monitor which one blinks first, as the loser of that battle could drop out quickly and affect the positions of horses trying to track them.

Tip Foster has had 83 days between runs and is trained by a yard (Barron, T14: 0/6) that has not placed a horse in the past 14 days — watch the market and parade for signs of readiness before elevating the chance.

Kody B and Trust Amy are genuine hold-up horses racing out of their preferred position due to field congestion at the rear — if either drifts wider than expected or gets shuffled back further, discount their chances further still.

Go Vince Go returns just 12 days after his last run; Easterby runs horses in quick succession when fit, so the bounce factor is low, but watch whether he travels as freely as he did when 3rd on similar ground recently.

Rogue Attraction's headgear flag and form of 0-0 in last two runs warrants watching in the paddock — if she shows freshness and Tudhope is positive from the outset, the 6f Good profile makes her a legitimate each-way threat from the hold-up group.

races.name: Ladies Night 2027 On Sale Now Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up 5-6f performer for Phillip Makin, but aged nine and form figures on Good ground show a limited 5/15 sim-going record with no wins; Sam James takes the ride but the pace scenario gives this horse little to aim at from the rear.

runners_data.name: Cape Sovereign
runners_data.note: 315 days off the track is a major concern — Daniel Tudhope is an asset and Rebecca Menzies has had no runners strike in the last fortnight; sim-going record of 9/13 on turf with zero wins in this going suggests ring-rustiness is likely to tell.

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good turf over 5f in recent history for Julie Camacho; Ryan Sexton rides and the visor has been applied consistently — 22 days since last run is manageable, and this horse's profile suits a scenario where the pace quickens and a midfield run becomes viable.

runners_data.name: Hvar
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a poor sim-going record (2/8) and no wins or places on Good turf in this form string; Jason Hart rides for John & Sean Quinn who have had a productive fortnight (3/16), but the form figures (-00709) are discouraging and 52 days off is notable.

runners_data.name: Without Flaw
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, confirmed by a recent 5f Good-ground win at this course; Joanna Mason takes the ride for Tina Jackson and the sim-going record (11/15) is strong — the STYLE_FIT flag notes she is technically styled as Prominent, but she functionally leads and is the pivotal pace-control horse here.

runners_data.name: Harry Mole
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello partners this consistent 5f Good-ground performer for Steph Hollinshead; four runner-up finishes in the last five starts on this going and trip make him a natural sit-and-pounce type, and his profile is perfectly aligned with the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Cotai Starlight
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott takes the ride for Katie Scott on this three-year-old who won over 6f on Good ground recently; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, the field's congestion means Stott will be doing well to find a clean midfield berth rather than his natural late position — style fit is tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Brian Rothwell's six-year-old ran just three days ago, which is a significant fitness flag; tongue-tie and cheekpiece combination in place, and while this horse has winning form on Good 5f turf, the true closer profile means it is operating outside its comfort zone in a race without genuine pace to chase.

runners_data.name: Never Dark
runners_data.note: Aged nine and a true hold-up horse for Iain Jardine — Alex Jary claims 3lb, which helps the weight, but the sim-going record (9/15) and form string (-66726) suggest modest ability in this grade; running out of natural position makes this difficult to place confidently.

runners_data.name: Crafty Spirit
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh's mount carries a hood and has two recent wins on Good turf over 5f for John Wainwright — genuinely strong form figures (3,1,1,2 in last four on suitable going); a true closer by nature, placed into midfield by the map due to hold-up congestion, but has the form to compete if it can manoeuvre.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine runs this three-year-old six days after its last start — one win and two places on Good turf from seven runs; Andrew Mullen rides, and the sim-going record (3/7) is acceptable, but a true closer dropped into midfield means the chance is structurally compromised in a single-led, moderate-pace race.

runners_data.name: Keep The Gold
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this four-year-old who wears a hood; Michael Dods sends out three winners in 21 recent runners and the form shows a recent 2nd on Good 5f turf — a hold-up horse by trade, its best chance comes if the tempo picks up, which the pace map suggests is unlikely.

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: P J McDonald takes the reins on this seven-year-old prominent racer for Rebecca Menzies, wearing tongue-tie and cheekpiece; the sim-going record (10/15) is moderate but the natural racing style as a genuine prominent type means McDonald can look to track Without Flaw and contest for position — a legitimate place contender in the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for R Mike Smith, ridden by apprentice Rhys Elliott (5lb claim), ran just three days ago; tongue-tie, cheekpiece, and hood all applied, and while the horse has place form on Good 5f ground, a true hold-up style mapped to midfield and a quick turnaround combine to weaken the case.

races.paceDynamic: Without Flaw is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, on Good ground over Carlisle's sharp 5f, is likely to stride straight into an uncontested lead from the outset, setting a rhythm that is sustainable rather than frenetic. Harry Mole and Kyber Crystal are the two genuine prominent types who will look to track closely, meaning the early order is relatively orderly with no serious challenger looking to burn Without Flaw off the front. The bulk of this field — Cotai Starlight, Supremissy, Opal Storm, Never Dark, Crafty Spirit, Keep The Gold, and Royal Duke — are true hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply far more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of those, Cotai Starlight and Crafty Spirit are most likely to physically secure the best midfield berths given their recent course-and-distance form. A controlled, single-led gallop on Good turf over five furlongs at Carlisle strongly favours prominent racers who can make ground from just off the pace in the straight, and genuinely late closers face an uphill battle in a race not likely to be run at a searching enough tempo to burn off front-end rivals.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Without Flaw bowls along unchallenged and the pace is fair-to-moderate, allowing Harry Mole or Kyber Crystal to strike from close range.
scenarios.body: Without Flaw dictates a measured gallop and the finish becomes a sprint for those sitting just off the leader, rewarding horses with tactical speed over raw finishing ability. Harry Mole's consistent proximity form (three runner-up finishes on Good ground over this trip) makes him the archetypal beneficiary, with Kyber Crystal also capable of picking up from the prominent position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Without Flaw secures a completely uncontested lead and the pace is comfortable enough that she never comes off the bridle until the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Without Flaw's most recent run was a win over this exact course, distance, and going, and a soft enough pace means she simply never gets run out of it — her fieldcraft on this track is her biggest asset. The prominent horses get into a race for second as the leader proves beyond catching.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Early, Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Mole or Kyber Crystal pushes forward to contest the early lead and a genuine tempo develops, opening the race up for midfield horses.
scenarios.body: A quicker gallop burns off the front two and creates a gap for a horse able to finish strongly from midfield, which on the flat 5f course at Carlisle is a meaningful opportunity. Bibendum, a genuine 5f Good-ground winner in recent form, and Crafty Spirit, who has won twice on Good turf over this trip, are best placed of the midfield runners to capitalise, though their redistributed stablemates face structural disadvantages getting clear runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough throughout to leave the field vulnerable to a horse produced from off the bridle in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely outcome given only one front-runner controls proceedings and a moderate tempo is most probable, but Cotai Starlight or Supremissy could theoretically thread through if gaps appear late. Both are true closers operating out of their natural position here, and the style-fit discount is real — this scenario depends on conditions that the race shape is unlikely to produce.

watchPoints.text: Without Flaw is the only horse likely to lead — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged from the gate, the entire field must account for her at the business end of a 5f Good-ground contest.

Harry Mole has been runner-up four times in his last five starts on Good 5f ground — watch whether Dougie Costello gets the jump on Kyber Crystal for the prominent position just behind the leader, as that berth could be decisive.

Bibendum is the hold-up horse with the most compelling recent form (two 5f Good-ground wins for Julie Camacho) — watch whether the visor-wearing five-year-old gets a clear run from midfield, as track congestion with 14 runners at Carlisle over 5f is a real tactical risk.

Cape Sovereign's 315-day absence is an obvious concern, but Daniel Tudhope is capable of producing a freshened horse — watch the market for any late support that might suggest stable confidence on seasonal reappearance.

Opal Storm ran just three days ago and Crafty Spirit also has a recent run behind it — monitor both for any visible signs of fatigue or sluggishness in the preliminaries, as quick turnarounds on Good ground at this level can expose horses who have not recovered fully.

races.name: Racing Again Wednesday 9th Sept Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Hill O Rue
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott partners this Kevin Ryan-trained 4yo who is a genuine hold-up horse; 52 days since last run is a mild flag, and similar-going form reads 6 runs for no wins and 2 places, suggesting this trip and conditions are not a banker proposition even if the closing run arrives.|

runners_data.name: Dr Rio
runners_data.note: A 10yo veteran trained by Declan Carroll, last seen 15 days ago with a string of consistent form; runs from deep and has a solid record on Good ground (12 from 15 on similar going) but at OR 59 with advancing age, finding the front is the challenge in a race Hansteen controls from the front.|

runners_data.name: Taylormade Lad
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's 4yo has placed three times in similar Going and showed well over 11-12f; Connor Beasley keeps the ride and this horse's natural hold-up style means it needs the pace to be honest enough to deliver its late kick — form of 33557 shows consistency without dominance.|

runners_data.name: Vampire Slayer

races.paceDynamic: Hansteen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, he should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over this 1m3f trip at Carlisle, controlling tempo entirely on his own terms. His recent form string of -02122 shows he is thoroughly comfortable making the running at this level, and on Good ground at a track that suits patient, rhythm-based front-running, he can dictate a sustainable gallop that will not burn him off early. The hold-up contingent — Hill O Rue, Dr Rio, Taylormade Lad and others — will be chasing from some way back, meaning their closing runs depend entirely on Hansteen not getting too far clear too soon. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles and any horse capable of tracking Hansteen closely, as the true closers face a significant positional deficit against an uncontested pacer on fair ground. Several horses in this field — Vampire Slayer, Off Spin, Due To Shine, Speechman and Star Of Markinch — are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield simply because the rear of the field is overcrowded; of those, Vampire Slayer and Off Spin are most likely to actually push forward and secure a tracking position, though neither will trouble Hansteen for the lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hansteen Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen leads without any meaningful pressure and controls a steady-to-fair gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Hansteen sets a comfortable tempo into the final two furlongs and his rivals cannot close the gap he has built, leaving him to score or force others to burn petrol chasing him down; Riddikulus, tracking closely from a prominent position, is ideally placed to pounce if Hansteen ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen sets honest but not excessive pace and a prominent-held runner delivers a well-timed challenge inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A horse like Riddikulus or Off Spin, sitting just off the leader throughout, uses the even tempo to mount a smooth challenge without needing to make up ground from far back; this shape rewards runners who travel well in transit rather than those finishing from deep.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen sets a genuinely strong pace that strings the field out and leaves him vulnerable late.
scenarios.body: The sustained effort tires Hansteen inside the final furlong and a hold-up horse with a powerful finish — Taylormade Lad or Hill O Rue — collects late; this scenario requires pace genuinely honest enough to set up the closers, which is uncertain with only one pace-setter.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen misses the break or is pulled up early, fragmenting the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Without a clear leader, several hold-up horses are stranded out of position and the race becomes chaotic with no horse suited to the shape that emerges; a horse like Vampire Slayer, who has the tactical flexibility and form over staying trips, could capitalise on the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Riddikulus is the primary danger to Hansteen — if Oliver Stammers positions him just off the leader's heels from the outset, he has the Good-ground form and two wins over 10-12f to deliver a strong tracking challenge inside the final two furlongs.

Vampire Slayer's 160-day absence is the biggest unknown in the race — watch how sharply it comes out of the stalls; if it travels fluently into midfield early it remains a dark horse, but ring-rustiness over a trip shorter than its recent wins is a real risk.

Hansteen's pace control is the spine of this race shape — if Jason Hart is forced to set a genuinely strong tempo by any unexpected early pressure from the redistributed hold-up types (Off Spin or Vampire Slayer pushing forward), the closing runners' chances improve materially.

Star Of Markinch has finished fourth in four of its last five starts across Good ground — a pattern of consistent near-miss form that suggests each-way interest but also a horse that rarely delivers the decisive finishing effort needed to win.

Taylormade Lad's form of 3-3-5-5-7 in recent runs shows it is finding the frame less often over time; Connor Beasley's record with the horse and today's 1m3f trip on Good are the best available conditions for this yard, so a step forward is plausible but not assured.

races.paceDynamic: Hey Havana is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival willing or able to push up and challenge for the lead, P J McDonald can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, likely setting a sustainable, honest gallop on Good ground over 1m3f at Carlisle. Falaise Blanc is the only other horse with any prominent inclination and may press forward to sit just off the pace, but the rest of the field — Annandale, Lightning Galaxy, Zebra Star, Alcanzor and others — are natural hold-up types, most of whom have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is no room at the rear for all of them. This creates a race where Hey Havana controls the narrative from the front, the midfield is congested with horses racing at least partially out of their preferred role, and the closing stages will likely be a sustained stamina test rather than a sprint finish. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently behind the leader or grind relentlessly from mid-division — pure late-closers will face the challenge of making ground against a well-regulated pace without the benefit of a true end-to-end gallop to exploit. Several runners tagged as redistributed — Annandale, Lightning Galaxy, Zebra Star and Alcanzor — are true hold-up types who cannot all drop to the rear, meaning Annandale, the most experienced and form-consistent of them, is best placed to find a viable closing position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hey Havana Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana settles into an uncontested lead and dictates a fair but not punishing gallop, allowing McDonald to conserve energy before kicking from the front.
scenarios.body: Hey Havana has shown the ability to front-run and place second or thereabouts consistently, and on Good ground at this trip with no genuine pace rival to unsettle him, he can simply dictate and prove hard to peg back; Falaise Blanc, sitting closest in second, is the main beneficiary as a prominent type with solid each-way form at this trip and going.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana sets enough of a gallop that a horse sitting second or third can reel him in over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Falaise Blanc has a strong record of placing prominently on Good ground at Carlisle-type trips and carries strong each-way claims as the horse most likely to be on Hey Havana's shoulder turning in; Annandale, despite being a natural hold-up type, has winning and placing form specifically at 1m3f on Good going and, if the redistribution allows him a forward enough position, he could emerge as the most dangerous of the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Rush From Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana goes hard enough early that the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile, opening a gap for a genuine closer to storm through.
scenarios.body: Idyllic has the most realistic hold-up profile of the non-redistributed closers in this field and has shown course-and-distance awareness at this sort of trip on comparable going, giving her the best chance of finishing fast if the tempo suits; Annandale's five-run sequence at 1m1f-1m3f on Good ground is the strongest closing form in the race, and if he finds the space his natural style demands, he becomes a threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Midfield Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield causes interference or traffic issues and the result is compressed, negating pace advantages.
scenarios.body: With multiple redistributed hold-up types forced into the same midfield bracket — Annandale, Lightning Galaxy, Zebra Star and Alcanzor all competing for the same ground — a scrappy, bunched finish is a live if minority possibility; Falaise Blanc, sitting clear of the mess in a prominent position, and Hey Havana, already ahead of the chaos, are best insulated from midfield trouble.

watchPoints.text: Hey Havana is handed an uncontested lead by default — if P J McDonald finds the right tempo, this horse will be very difficult to catch at the top of the straight and punters must assess whether the 1m3f trip is within his stamina range.

Falaise Blanc is the one horse best positioned to track Hey Havana and pounce — watch whether Jake Dickson (5lb claim) settles the horse immediately behind the leader rather than allowing a gap to form, as the late ground on Good has consistently been this horse's friend.

Annandale, Zebra Star, Lightning Galaxy and Alcanzor are all true hold-up types forced into the same midfield corridor — watch for crowding and potential traffic issues on the long run from the back straight into the straight at Carlisle, which could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.

Rory's Gold's form on Good going has been uniformly poor compared to the one Soft-ground second — if the going description is firm enough on the day to shade Good-to-Firm, that pattern becomes even more of a negative signal for Amie Waugh's partner.

Farabove The Limit has never run at 1m3f and Sam James must decide whether to ride handily or drop in — given the congested midfield, either choice carries risk, and the horse's record suggests it has yet to demonstrate the stamina to truly see out this trip.
